note: P4336 (Pro 28:27) — who gives to the poor will not want; who hides his eyes gets many a curse.

dims.v: generosity — the open hand that never wants
the giving to the poor of the generous man who therefore will not want — the open hand that God supplies, the opposite of the one who hides his eyes from need
the callous hiding it is set against (266678)
set against the shut eyes that earn many curses
natan (give) — 'whoever GIVES to the poor will not want' (cf 11:24-25; 19:17); the generous never lack, for God supplies the open hand. Emergent: generosity to the poor as the way to never wanting.
callous blindness — willfully not seeing the poor's need, and cursed for it
the hiding of the eyes from the poor's need — the willful blindness that refuses to see suffering, and so earns many a curse, the opposite of the open hand that is supplied
the generosity it is set against (266674)
set against the giving hand that never wants

alam (hide/conceal) — 'but he who HIDES his eyes will get many a curse'; to look away from the poor's need is a cursed callousness. Emergent: willful blindness to suffering as a cursed refusal of mercy (cf 21:13).
